author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Merrimack native Mickey Gasper hit his ninth home run of the season Friday night, continuing a breakout run with the Boston Red Sox. Gasper connected in the fifth inning against the Kansas City Royals at Fenway Park, cutting Boston’s deficit to two runs and giving another lift to a player whose rise has become a point of pride for New Hampshire baseball fans.

The homer came one day after Gasper spent Boston’s day off at a youth clinic in Peabody, Massachusetts. He worked with children from a baseball club that he belonged to while growing up in the Granite State. The appearance followed an unusually compressed stretch for the Red Sox, who had played 14 games over 13 days before Thursday’s break.

Gasper’s path from Merrimack youth baseball to Fenway has supplied a distinctly regional thread to Boston’s season. Friday’s result added a measurable milestone: nine major-league home runs this season. His decision to use the club’s brief pause for a youth clinic also linked his current role with the program that helped shape him, placing the latest on-field moment beside a direct investment in the next generation of local players.
dek: The New Hampshire native homered at Fenway Park one day after using Boston’s rare day off to work with young baseball players.
headline: Merrimack’s Mickey Gasper hits ninth home run of season
